messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started rwd-service@v2.14.0 -> prod (canary=5%) - job id 5562. Config change: enable feature flag `dynamic-batching` on inference path.
jamie: Confirming - I see the canary kicked off at ~now. Quick check on dashboard.
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for rwd-service.prod - 503s rising from 0.12% -> 2.8% in 3m :rotating_light:
priya: I'm paged and looking. Which customers hit?
mike: Logs show bunch of `kvcache: mismatch` errors in the runtime, restarted streams failing with 503. Started ~ just after canary deploy logs show sequence TLs: `kvcache_seq_mismatch`
jamie: Rolling traces — p99 latency also jumped from 180ms -> 1.6s for chat/generation routes. Affected primarily hosted API region us-west-2.
priya: Reproduced locally with canary binary using dynamic-batching on; appears to drop KV cache continuity for multi-chunk requests.
jamie: What are mitigation options? Can we flip the feature flag?
mike: We can flip ff via `ffcli` quickly. If that doesn't help, abort canary/rollback.
sarah: Noted customer impact: some high-throughput customers on hosted API reporting partial responses/timeouts. No data leak. Severity: potential SLO breach and customer-facing failures.
priya: I'm going to `ffcli set dynamic-batching false --env prod` now. Will monitor metrics.
jamie: :eyes: do it. Also mark canary paused in console.
priya: (runs) `ffcli set dynamic-batching false --env prod` -> success. Feature flag disabled at 3 hosts in canary pool, propagation started.
incident-bot: NOTE: Feature flag change recorded by audit (id ff-9832).
mike: Metric update: 503 rate dropping in canary cohort but still elevated cluster-wide due to routing mix.
jamie: Can we abort the rollout? I want to stop further ramp.
sarah: Abort recommended. deploy-bot, abort canary job 5562.
deploy-bot: Received abort request for job 5562. Initiating canary rollback -> stopping further traffic.
jamie: After abort, traffic should route to previous stable variant. Watching latency and errors.
priya: Post-abort stats: canary hosts still draining - KV errors falling to baseline. p99 back to ~220ms. Customer errors down.
mike: I'll trigger an automated cache-warm on the stable pool to avoid cold-prefix problems: `rwd infra cache-warm --targets stable-pool --pattern chat/*`
sarah: Good. Also opening an incident ticket: INC-2026-1843, severity P1->P2 after rollback and mitigation. I'll add impact notes and customers to notify.
jamie: Assigning follow-up to eng-runtime and deploy owners. Need a rollback postmortem and test for KV continuity with dynamic-batching.
priya: Quick postmortem notes: root cause likely batching change that altered request boundaries and invalidated KV cache sequence numbers when streaming + batching combined.
mike: I'll put a temporary gating rule: block dynamic-batching flag for prod until we have a KV-compat shim or spec update.
oncall-next: Taking handoff for next shift. Please add runbook steps and link traces.
sarah: Oncall handoff: summary in INC-2026-1843, actions done: ff toggled off, canary aborted, cache-warm, rollback confirmed. Tags: rollback, feature-flag, canary, kvcache.
priya: Leaving a quick checklist: 1) confirm all canary instances removed from LB, 2) verify no 503 spikes in last 10m, 3) coordinate regression test for kv-seq with qa.
jamie: Thanks all. If anything resurfaces ping here and escalate to SRE pager. Otherwise we'll treat as mitigated and track fix in next patch. :white_check_mark:
